name: Alpha 10 Hz parieto-occipital sine (tACS target)
origin: Project construct after alpha tACS studies by the Herrmann group (Oldenburg: Zaehle 2010, Kasten 2016) and Helfrich 2014 (Hamburg, with Herrmann)
summary: A 10 Hz magnetic sine for 20 min over P7, Oz and P8, near the parieto-occipital cortex where transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) studies report alpha effects. Those studies drove electric current through scalp electrodes: 0.8 V/m in cortex at 2 mA, against about 1 uV/m induced here. The magnetic version is this project's own design, and nobody has tested it.
notes: The sources are electrical: tACS drives current through scalp electrodes. Only Helfrich 2014 used a fixed 10 Hz for 20 min, with electrodes over Cz and Oz (p.2), and reported phase-dependent detection. Zaehle 2010 stimulated for 10 min at each person's individual alpha frequency (IAF) through PO9/PO10 (p.3) and reported higher alpha afterwards (10 active vs 10 sham). Kasten 2016 ran 20 min at the IAF (p.1); the difference between active and sham vanished after about 70 min. No source describes a magnetic 10 Hz exposure. This program plays a 10 Hz sine on three coils in phase with equal weight, at P7, Oz and P8 (CH4 to CH6 of the ring layout); the other channels stay silent. The 20 min at 10 Hz is one study's setting (Helfrich). The coil sites are this project's choice; O1, O2 or Pz are possible custom alternatives. If you have measured your IAF (8 to 13 Hz), set f0 to it. The sources state a current, not a magnetic field: transcranial current at 2 mA reaches 0.8 V/m in cortex (Huang 2017 p.1). These coils induce about 1 uV/m, a factor of 8 x 10^5 less, so no entrainment by induction is expected. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Nobody has tested the magnetic version. If alpha entrainment is the goal, the evidence is for electrical tACS, a different device with its own safety requirements and outside this helmet. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on discomfort.
setting: Seated, eyes open or closed as in the study you follow (Kasten 2016: 20 min).
schedule: A single 20-min session; for a self-test, compare it with sham using the app's Blind option on separate days.
source: Zaehle et al. 2010, PLoS One https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2967471/ ; Helfrich et al. 2014, Curr Biol https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24461998/ ; Kasten et al. 2016, Front Hum Neurosci https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4879138/ ; Huang et al. 2017, eLife (transcranial electric field in humans) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28169833/
